raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Per-tensor FP8 attention with paged K/V and a per-head sink is declined even though the SM100 D64/D128 kernel already has the paged loader and the sink epilogue. Admit that composition in graph support checking and the standalone API, and update the support matrix.

The added tests cover packed and unpacked GQA, MHA, independently laid-out K/V pools, both FP8 input formats, output formats and optional Stats, causal/window masks, empty KV and trimmed Q. A retained CUDA graph is replayed after rebinding storage and changing sinks, lengths and page-table contents; outputs are poisoned before replay. D128 replay covers both CTA widths.

## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of LICENSE.txt.
- [x] I ran pre-commit and committed formatting changes.
- [x] I checked the applicable AGENTS.md rules, including Python Rules 1–8 and SDPA Rule S2.
- [x] Required change-type, affected-area and originator labels are applied.

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL — SDPA capability admission and regression tests.

## API and compatibility impact

Existing graph and standalone signatures are unchanged. SM100-line per-tensor FP8 D64/D128 paged plans now accept attention sinks. The existing FP8 split-plus-sink restriction remains, as it does for dense KV; paged THD queries and block-scaled outputs retain their existing restrictions.

## Testing

Coverage lives in `test/python/sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_fwd_paged_sm100.py`, including `test_paged_graph_fp8_sink` and `test_paged_graph_fp8_sink_rebind_replay`. Run the per-tensor FP8 subset with:

```sh
cd test/python
pytest -q -o addopts= -m L0 sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_fwd_paged_sm100.py -k 'fp8 and not mxfp8'
```

Pre-commit passes for all four changed files. The regression first demonstrates the missing plan on the parent implementation; candidate checks compare O, Stats and Amax_O against the existing FP64 reference and check exact-zero dead rows.

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `9b30347570f3` against base `fc20f4702ec9`.

The paged FP8 sink composition passed focused GPU and standalone checks. One existing admission test still expects the removed rejection and needs an update.

**[P2] Update the existing paged FP8 sink admission assertion** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/9b30347570f3b5c57be937c456c0d90fda756cdf/test/python/sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_graph_analyzer.py#L2550))

test_paged_quantized_rows_mismatch_reasons still checks that mismatch(..., has_sink=True) contains 'attention sink'. This PR correctly returns None, so the test raises TypeError and fails the SDPA suite. Change this assertion to expect admission, and retain a separate rejection check for an explicit split-plus-sink plan.

Evidence: The existing test fails locally at line 2550 with TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable. The independent standalone probe confirms split_kv=2 with a sink remains rejected. Attribution: New regression in an existing test caused by the intended admission change.

Validation: 69 paged per-tensor FP8 tests passed on SM100, including the 19 new sink and changed-input CUDA Graph replay cases. O, Stats and Amax were checked against the FP64 reference. Two independent multi-wave cases passed: D64/cga1/packed and D128/cga2/unpacked, E5M2 inputs, BF16 output, independent K/V layouts, empty and trimmed rows, extreme sink values and a sliding window. Graph and standalone outputs agreed exactly; both rejected split-plus-sink plans. Three eager repeats per independent case matched O, Stats and Amax bitwise after output reset. Reused CI pipeline 76728788. Its runtime and test files match this head; the later commit only changes documentation. CI is pending.

Limitations: Local GPU checks cover SM100. Other platforms remain subject to CI. Repeatability checks cover fixed configurations, not cross-device or batch invariance.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.
